name: Exostoses-anetodermia-brachydactyly type E syndrome
aliases: Exostoses with anetodermia and brachydactyly type E

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Exostoses-anetodermia-brachydactyly type E syndrome diagnostic criteria

criteria.description: Presence of multiple osteochondromas (exostoses) primarily affecting long bones
Cutaneous anetodermia characterized by localized areas of slack, wrinkled skin due to loss of elastic tissue
Brachydactyly type E involving shortening of metacarpals and metatarsals
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Radiographic evidence of exostoses and brachydactyly

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: multiple exostoses, anetodermia lesions, and brachydactyly type E
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by radiographic findings; genetic testing may assist but no specific gene identified

searchTerms: type E short fingers and toes
specific short digit pattern type E

imaging: Radiographs showing multiple osteochondromas on long bones
X-rays demonstrating brachydactyly type E with shortened metacarpals/metatarsals
genetic: No specific gene mutation identified; suspected autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
other: Skin biopsy showing loss of elastic fibers consistent with anetodermia

distinguishingFeatures: Brachydactyly type E without exostoses or skin abnormalities

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of exostoses suggesting malignant transformation
Neurological deficits indicating nerve compression by exostoses
Ulceration or infection over skin lesions
references: Orphanet: Exostoses-anetodermia-brachydactyly type E syndrome - ORPHA:1962
